Correct only the three explicitly selected fields. Preserve the entire accepted interface and all unrelated operations, objectives, bindings, scopes, choices, budgets and cleanup.

The compiler already accepts the retained TaskPlan, but /outputs/rows fails the accepted maxItems:10 contract because flatten conservatively returns an unbounded array. A read-only compile of these exact two binding changes preserves the row item contract and produces maxItems:10 without inference or new operators:
1. In extract_product_row.resultType, keep the outer object and its required member named rows. Replace ONLY rows.type (currently an array with minItems=maxItems=1) with its existing non-null object items type. This yields exactly one row object per actual visited product. Preserve required nom, description, prix, status; the first three remain nullable strings, status remains a non-null string. Do not change the accepted public rows array.
2. Replace finalize_rows.outputs.rows.value (currently flatten of output(scrape_products,rows)) with its existing single operand: {kind:"output",source:"scrape_products",port:"rows"}, with all unrelated optional fields absent/null/empty according to the issued schema. The loop already bounds and collects at most ten row objects; no second flatten or inference is needed.
3. Set open_product_page.requires to the typed predicate not_equal(field(item,"href"), null). The current-page read behavior of a null URL must not silently substitute for visiting the selected product. This is an explicit local runtime precondition, not a new permission or inferred condition proof.

Return only the authorized typed patch. No new tasks, broad plan rewrite, invented values, widened constraints, requirement edits, truncation or new mechanisms.
